descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT OAT-06 tests 5-6; TFA-94514 req 6, 7 · “notes generated, handoffs sent, and time from Pre-Round opened to note complete, aggregated and queryable in Convex”. Mixed: stated part — Per-day row: opens, notes completed, open-to-complete minutes, notes generated in both modes; every AI call logs provider time; our part — A device on a wrong date/zone and an encounter across local midnight (3.8 applied to analytics days), regenerate counting (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-07/S28, TC-08/S20

Approach · OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · S10 The per-day row through the screens: 0 / 1 / many opens, a timed encounter, a regenerate, Nursing Home notes, a second device on the wrong date and zone, an encounter across local midnight

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U6 Completing an encounter fires both timestamps (Pre-Round summary opened, note marked complete), and they aggregate per physician per day (UAT OAT-06 Test 5; UAT 3.3; TFA-94514 AC 4)
  • U7 Per physician per day: notes generated, handoffs sent, and time from Pre-Round opened to note complete are aggregated and queryable in Convex (UAT OAT-06 Test 6; TFA-94514 AC 6)
  • U13 Every AI call (pre-round summary, note generation, billing, Ask AI, photo capture, handoff) logs its total time and, separately, the time the AI provider itself took, and which model answered (UAT 3.5; UAT 3.9; TFA-94514 AC 7)
  • U14 Per-day aggregation follows the server clock: a device with a wrong date, no clock set or another time zone files its events on the same day as any other device (UAT 3.8)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Fresh physician with Hospital patients A (note-ready with a note), B (encounter dictation typed by the agent), C and D (note-ready with notes) and one Nursing Home resident; T0 and the day's rollup read at T0. Browser context 1 on the correct clock; …

When R1 Hospital (context 1): open A, leave, open A again; open B; open the resident; wait 2 minutes and Mark Encounter Complete on A; on B tap Generate, then Generate again (a regenerate). R2 Nursing Home: open the resident -> Encounter -> type a visit dictation -> Generate; …

Then R1 hospital row: preRoundSummariesOpened +2 (A, B), notesCompleted +1, encountersTimed +1, minutesPreRoundToComplete + A's minutesFromPreRoundOpened (>= 2), notesGenerated >= 1 for B; the day's average (minutesPreRoundToComplete / encountersTimed) is readable from the row. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-06 Test 5 and 6 + TFA-94514 AC 4/AC 6, UAT 3.8, and 3.5/3.9 + AC 7 for the AI calls: post-run read of usage:_dailyForActor equals the T0 values plus the judged deltas. Judged: R1 opens +2 (one per chart opened), A timed with minutes >= 2, notesGenerated >= 1 for B; R2 nursing_home +1 after the first visit; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S10 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.
